name: Tag out-of-stock products, hide them after X days, and restore them when back in stock
docs:
Tags active products that can't be bought, hides them after a set number of days, and brings them back when stock returns. Nothing is ever deleted.

Every hour, and whenever you run the task manually:

1. An active product with no sellable variant gets the out-of-stock tag. The time is saved in the `mechanic.out_of_stock_since` metafield.
2. If it still can't be bought after the configured number of days, it is set to Draft or Unlisted, and the time is saved in `mechanic.out_of_stock_hidden_at`.
3. When a tagged product can be bought again, the tag is removed. If this task hid it, it is set back to Active.

Step 3 also runs as soon as Shopify reports a stock increase, so restocked products come back within moments instead of waiting for the next hourly scan.

A product is sellable when at least one variant is available for sale: stock above zero at any location, or "Continue selling when out of stock" turned on.

This task leaves these products alone:

* Archived products
* Drafts this task did not create
* Products with the "never hide" tag (they still get the out-of-stock tag)
* Products someone set back to Active by hand after this task hid them, until they are back in stock

**Draft or Unlisted?** A Draft product's page returns a 404. An Unlisted product keeps its page (with noindex) but disappears from collections, search, recommendations and the sitemap.

**Safety stop:** if more than 70% of active products look out of stock, the run stops with an error and changes nothing, because a broken stock sync is the likelier cause.

**Test mode** is on by default: the task only logs what it would do. Turn it off once the log looks right.

Use Shopify API version 2026-07 or newer (Advanced mode, below the code), which Unlisted requires.
